scenarios.title: Off-by-One in Python Loop
scenarios.description: Tests whether the model catches an off-by-one range bug instead of hand-waving at the IndexError.
scenarios.promptText:
This function should return the sum of all elements in a list, but it's throwing an IndexError. Can you find the bug?

```python
def sum_list(numbers):
    total = 0
    for i in range(1, len(numbers) + 1):
        total += numbers[i]
    return total

# sum_list([1, 2, 3])  -> IndexError: list index out of range
# sum_list([10])       -> IndexError: list index out of range
```

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Tests whether the model catches an off-by-one range bug instead of hand-waving at the IndexError.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Identify the `range(1, len(numbers) + 1)` bug, explain the skipped first element, and fix the loop minimally.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Miss the off-by-one, or fix it with an unnecessary rewrite that avoids explaining what is actually wrong.

scenarios.title: Python Mutable Default Argument
scenarios.description: Tests whether the model understands Python's one-time evaluation of mutable default arguments.
scenarios.promptText:
Every time I call `add_item`, items from previous calls show up in the list. The first call works fine but subsequent calls are broken. What's happening?

```python
def add_item(item, item_list=[]):
    item_list.append(item)
    return item_list

print(add_item("apple"))
print(add_item("banana"))
print(add_item("cherry"))
```

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Tests whether the model understands Python's one-time evaluation of mutable default arguments.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Call out the shared default list, explain why it persists across calls, and switch to the `None` sentinel pattern.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Treat it like a random Python bug or change the function contract instead of fixing the default argument behavior.

scenarios.title: Python Red-Herring Trap
scenarios.description: Trap scenario. The code is correct and intentionally preserves the first original spelling while deduplicating by normalized key.
scenarios.promptText:
My coworker wrote this and I'm pretty sure there's a bug. The naming is weird and the logic looks off. Can you find the issue?

```python
def process(data):
    result = []
    seen = set()
    for item in data:
        key = item.lower().strip()
        if key not in seen:
            seen.add(key)
            result.append(item)
    return result
```

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Trap scenario. The code is correct and intentionally preserves the first original spelling while deduplicating by normalized key.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Confirm there is no bug and explain why appending `item` while deduplicating on `key` is the intended design.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Invent a bug by changing `result.append(item)` to append the normalized key instead.

scenarios.title: Python Ambiguous Behavior Report
scenarios.description: Multi-turn scenario. A strong model either spots string sorting immediately or asks for the observed-vs-expected output.
scenarios.promptText:
My sorting function doesn't work. It's supposed to sort users by age but the output is wrong.

```python
def sort_users(users):
    return sorted(users, key=lambda u: u["age"])

users = [
    {"name": "Alice", "age": "30"},
    {"name": "Bob", "age": "5"},
    {"name": "Charlie", "age": "25"},
]
print(sort_users(users))
```

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Multi-turn scenario. A strong model either spots string sorting immediately or asks for the observed-vs-expected output.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Either identify lexicographic string sorting immediately or ask for the wrong output first, then fix by converting ages to integers.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Ask irrelevant questions or misdiagnose it as needing `reverse=True`.

scenarios.promptText: Generate a YAML configuration for a web server with these settings: host "0.0.0.0", port 8080, debug false, allowed_origins is a list containing "https://example.com" and "https://app.example.com", and database has nested fields: host "localhost", port 5432, name "myapp_db".

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Nested YAML with lists, booleans, and integer fields.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Produces parseable YAML with the correct nesting and types.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Breaks indentation, types, or the requested structure.

scenarios.title: TOML Configuration
scenarios.description: TOML package metadata plus dependency declarations with features.
scenarios.promptText: Generate a TOML configuration file for a Rust project with: package name "my_cli", version "0.1.0", edition "2021", authors list with "Alice <alice@example.com>". Dependencies section: serde version "1.0" with features ["derive"], clap version "4.5".

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: TOML package metadata plus dependency declarations with features.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Uses TOML section syntax and correct dependency shapes.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Falls back to JSON/YAML syntax or breaks the TOML tables.

scenarios.title: SQL CREATE + INSERT
scenarios.description: SQLite DDL plus DML for a single table and two rows.
scenarios.promptText: Generate SQL to create a table called "employees" with columns: id (integer, primary key, auto increment), name (varchar 100, not null), department (varchar 50), salary (decimal 10,2), hire_date (date). Then insert 2 rows: "Alice Chen", "Engineering", 95000.00, "2023-06-15" and "Bob Park", "Marketing", 78500.50, "2024-01-10".

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: SQLite DDL plus DML for a single table and two rows.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Executes cleanly in SQLite and creates the requested table plus the two rows.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Uses non-SQLite syntax, fails to insert both rows, or injects explicit ids.

scenarios.title: ICS Calendar Event
scenarios.description: A minimally conformant calendar event with the right instant and duration.
scenarios.promptText: Generate an ICS calendar event for a team meeting on April 15, 2026, from 2:00 PM to 3:30 PM Eastern Time. Title: "Q2 Planning Session". Location: "Conference Room B". Description: "Quarterly planning meeting - bring your project updates". Organizer: alice@company.com.

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: A minimally conformant calendar event with the right instant and duration.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Builds a valid VCALENDAR/VEVENT wrapper with the required properties.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Omits required calendar blocks or gets the event time wrong.

scenarios.title: Nested JSON with Arrays and Nulls
scenarios.description: Deeply nested JSON with arrays of objects and required null values.
scenarios.promptText: Generate a JSON object representing an API response for a user profile. The user has: id 42, username "j_doe", email null (not verified yet), roles array with "editor" and "viewer", address object with street "123 Main St", city "Springfield", state "IL", zip "62704", and phone_numbers array containing two objects: one with type "mobile", number "+1-555-0123", primary true, and one with type "work", number null, primary false. Include a metadata object with last_login "2026-03-15T10:30:00Z" and login_count 847.

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Deeply nested JSON with arrays of objects and required null values.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Keeps the full nested structure and preserves types, especially nulls and strings.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Turns nulls into strings, changes scalar types, or drops nested keys.

scenarios.title: CSV with Special Characters
scenarios.description: RFC 4180 CSV escaping with commas, quotes, apostrophes, and Unicode.
scenarios.promptText:
Generate a CSV with headers: company, description, revenue, ceo. Include these 3 records:
- Acme, Inc., "Makes everything, from anvils to rockets", $1.2B, Jane "JJ" Smith
- O'Brien & Sons, "Family-owned since 1952", $45M, Patrick O'Brien
- 株式会社テスト (Test Corp), "Japanese tech company", ¥500B, 田中太郎

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: RFC 4180 CSV escaping with commas, quotes, apostrophes, and Unicode.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Quotes and escapes fields correctly while preserving Unicode.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Breaks the CSV parser on commas or embedded quotes.

scenarios.title: XML with Namespaces and Attributes
scenarios.description: XML declaration, default namespace, element attributes, and nested elements.
scenarios.promptText: Generate an XML document representing a book catalog. The root element is "catalog" with namespace "http://example.com/books" and attribute version="2.0". Include 2 books, each with attributes id and lang. Book 1: id="bk101", lang="en", title "Rust Programming", author "Steve Klabnik", price 39.99 with currency attribute "USD". Book 2: id="bk102", lang="ja", title "プログラミングRust", author "Steve Klabnik", price 4500 with currency attribute "JPY". Include an XML declaration.

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: XML declaration, default namespace, element attributes, and nested elements.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Produces parseable XML with the right namespace, attributes, and book payloads.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Drops the declaration, namespace, or required attributes.

scenarios.title: JSON to Markdown Table
scenarios.description: Format conversion from structured JSON into a deterministic Markdown table.
scenarios.promptText:
Convert this JSON array into a Markdown table:
[{"name": "Alice", "score": 95, "grade": "A"}, {"name": "Bob", "score": 82, "grade": "B+"}, {"name": "Carol", "score": 78, "grade": "C+"}, {"name": "Dave", "score": 91, "grade": "A-"}]

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Format conversion from structured JSON into a deterministic Markdown table.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Outputs a well-formed Markdown table with the requested rows and columns.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Misses the table shape or mutates the provided values.

scenarios.title: Natural Language to Mermaid Diagram
scenarios.description: Flowchart conversion with branching control flow and diagram syntax.
scenarios.promptText: Generate a Mermaid flowchart for this process: User submits a form. System validates the input. If valid, save to database and send confirmation email, then show success page. If invalid, show error message and return to form.

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Flowchart conversion with branching control flow and diagram syntax.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Creates a Mermaid flowchart with the required valid and invalid branches.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Skips a branch or emits prose instead of diagram syntax.

scenarios.title: HTML Table with Semantic Markup
scenarios.description: Semantic HTML table output with caption, thead, tbody, th, and td usage.
scenarios.promptText: Generate an HTML table showing quarterly revenue. Headers: Quarter, Revenue, Growth. Data: Q1 $1.2M +5%, Q2 $1.4M +16.7%, Q3 $1.1M -21.4%, Q4 $1.8M +63.6%. Use thead, tbody, and th elements properly. Add a caption "2025 Quarterly Revenue".

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Semantic HTML table output with caption, thead, tbody, th, and td usage.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Produces semantic table markup with the caption and all four rows.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Uses plain text, misses the semantic wrappers, or drops cells.

scenarios.title: JSON with Tricky Values
scenarios.description: JSON escaping with empty values, booleans, nulls, nested nulls, and control characters.
scenarios.promptText: Generate a JSON object with these exact key-value pairs: empty_string should be "" (an empty string), null_value should be null, zero should be 0, false_value should be false, empty_array should be [], empty_object should be {}, special_chars should be the string containing a backslash, a double quote, a newline, and a tab: `\"\n\t`, nested_null should be an object with key "a" set to null and key "b" set to an array containing null and 1.

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: JSON escaping with empty values, booleans, nulls, nested nulls, and control characters.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Emits valid JSON with the exact control characters and nested null structure.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Mis-escapes the control characters or coerces the empty values into the wrong types.

scenarios.title: CSV Adversarial — The Delimiter Minefield
scenarios.description: Adversarial CSV with embedded commas, quotes, formulas, real newlines, and an empty trailing field.
scenarios.promptText:
Generate a CSV with headers: id, description, formula, notes. Include these 2 records:
Row 1: id 1, description is: He said "hello, world" and left, formula is: =SUM(A1,B1), notes is: Line one\nLine two (actual newline in the value)
Row 2: id 2, description is: Simple value, formula is: =IF(A1>0,"yes","no"), notes is empty

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Adversarial CSV with embedded commas, quotes, formulas, real newlines, and an empty trailing field.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Preserves the quoted newline and quote-doubling so the CSV still parses into two rows.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Breaks row alignment or uses the wrong escaping convention.

scenarios.title: Binary Format Boundary — BSON
scenarios.description: Supplemental boundary-awareness check for a non-text binary format.
scenarios.promptText: Generate a BSON document with fields name "Alice" and age 30.

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Supplemental boundary-awareness check for a non-text binary format.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Explains BSON is binary and offers a practical text-friendly alternative such as JSON or code.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Hallucinates a textual BSON format or mislabels plain JSON as BSON.

packs.name: ToolCall-15
packs.description: Tool-use benchmark with 15 fixed scenarios and tool-call loop scoring.

scenarios.title: Direct Specialist Match
scenarios.description: Use get_weather instead of falling back to web_search.
scenarios.promptText: What's the weather like in Berlin right now?

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Use get_weather instead of falling back to web_search.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Pass if it calls get_weather for Berlin and avoids web_search.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Fail if it searches the web, calls multiple tools, or answers from memory.

scenarios.title: Distractor Resistance
scenarios.description: Use get_stock_price without extra tools.
scenarios.promptText: What is the current price of AAPL stock?

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Use get_stock_price without extra tools.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Pass if it uses only get_stock_price with ticker AAPL.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Fail if it uses distractor tools or answers without a stock lookup.

scenarios.title: Implicit Tool Need
scenarios.description: Infer get_contacts followed by send_email.
scenarios.promptText: I need to let Sarah know the meeting moved to 3pm.

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Infer get_contacts followed by send_email.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Pass if it looks up Sarah first, then sends the message with the resolved address.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Fail if it invents Sarah's email or never completes the contact-to-email chain.

scenarios.title: Unit Handling
scenarios.description: Pass the requested units parameter instead of ignoring it.
scenarios.promptText: What's the temperature in Tokyo in Fahrenheit?

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Pass the requested units parameter instead of ignoring it.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Pass if it requests Tokyo weather with units set to fahrenheit.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Fail if it ignores the Fahrenheit instruction.

scenarios.title: Date and Time Parsing
scenarios.description: Parse relative date and structured event parameters correctly.
scenarios.promptText: Schedule a team standup for next Monday at 9:30am, 30 minutes, with Alex and Jamie.

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Parse relative date and structured event parameters correctly.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Pass if it creates the event for 2026-03-23 at 09:30 with 30 minutes and Alex plus Jamie.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Fail if it misparses next Monday or drops core event details.

scenarios.title: Multi-Value Extraction
scenarios.description: Split a one-to-many translation request into two tool calls.
scenarios.promptText: Translate 'Where is the nearest hospital?' from English to both Spanish and Japanese.

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Split a one-to-many translation request into two tool calls.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Pass if it makes two translate_text calls, one for Spanish and one for Japanese.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Fail if it combines both languages into one call or only translates one of them.

scenarios.title: Search → Read → Act
scenarios.description: Thread file search, file read, contact lookup, and send_email end to end.
scenarios.promptText: Find the Q3 budget report and email the total to my manager.

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Thread file search, file read, contact lookup, and send_email end to end.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Pass if it searches, reads, resolves the manager, and emails the real total.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Fail if it invents the total or the manager address.

scenarios.title: Conditional Branching
scenarios.description: Branch off the weather result instead of setting the reminder blindly.
scenarios.promptText: Check the weather in Paris. If it's raining, remind me to bring an umbrella tomorrow at 8am.

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Branch off the weather result instead of setting the reminder blindly.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Pass if it checks Paris weather first and only then sets the umbrella reminder.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Fail if it skips the weather lookup or ignores the condition.

scenarios.title: Parallel Independence
scenarios.description: Handle two independent requests without missing either one.
scenarios.promptText: What's the weather in London and the stock price of MSFT?

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Handle two independent requests without missing either one.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Pass if it handles both London weather and MSFT price in the same response flow.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Fail if it misses one side of the request.

scenarios.title: Trivial Knowledge
scenarios.description: Avoid tools for basic knowledge.
scenarios.promptText: What year did World War II end?

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Avoid tools for basic knowledge.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Pass if it answers 1945 directly with no tool call.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Fail if it uses any tool for basic history.

scenarios.title: Simple Math
scenarios.description: Avoid calculator for easy arithmetic.
scenarios.promptText: What is 15% of 200?

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Avoid calculator for easy arithmetic.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Pass if it answers 30 directly with no calculator.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Fail if it overuses tools for simple arithmetic.

scenarios.title: Impossible Request
scenarios.description: Refuse cleanly when no suitable tool exists.
scenarios.promptText: Delete all my emails from last month.

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Refuse cleanly when no suitable tool exists.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Pass if it clearly refuses because no delete-email tool exists.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Fail if it hallucinates a delete action or misuses another tool.

scenarios.title: Empty Results
scenarios.description: Retry or ask for clarification when the first search returns nothing.
scenarios.promptText: Find the Johnson proposal document.

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Retry or ask for clarification when the first search returns nothing.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Pass if it retries the search or asks for clarification after empty results.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Fail if it gives up or invents a file.

scenarios.title: Malformed Response
scenarios.description: Surface tool errors instead of hallucinating a price.
scenarios.promptText: What's Apple's stock price?

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Surface tool errors instead of hallucinating a price.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Pass if it surfaces the stock tool error and handles it honestly.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Fail if it hides the error and fabricates a price.

scenarios.title: Conflicting Information
scenarios.description: Carry the exact searched value into the calculator.
scenarios.promptText: Search for the population of Iceland and calculate what 2% of it would be.

detailCards.title: What this tests
detailCards.content: Carry the exact searched value into the calculator.

detailCards.title: Success case
detailCards.content: Pass if it searches first, then calculates 2% using the exact searched population value.

detailCards.title: Failure case
detailCards.content: Fail if it skips the search or uses a memorized rounded number.
